evidence.title: Emily Wilson is retranslating 'The Odyssey' — all over again

occurrences.checkable_against: Christopher Nolan interviews and film development materials
occurrences.quote_span: Nolan had cited her translation and its opening sentence, “Tell me about a complicated man,” as inspiration for his epic film.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Emily Wilson

occurrences.checkable_against: Ancient Greek historical scholarship and Emily Wilson's public career records
occurrences.quote_span: Fame was of prime importance to the ancient Greeks, and Wilson is the rare classical scholar who has firsthand knowledge of a public life.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Emily Wilson

occurrences.checkable_against: Final manuscript and published new edition of The Odyssey
occurrences.quote_span: The new edition will be longer, she says, and will better reflect the differing social worlds of Homer’s poem.
occurrences.speaker: Emily Wilson
occurrences.subject: Emily Wilson

occurrences.checkable_against: Emily Wilson's 2017 translation and ancient Greek terminology
occurrences.quote_span: But she says her translation methods have become more sophisticated and that enough time has passed for her to see some flaws in her work — as an example, she overused the word “slave” when ancient Greek had different terms for different categories of enslaved people.
occurrences.speaker: Emily Wilson
occurrences.subject: Emily Wilson

occurrences.checkable_against: Christopher Nolan's public statements and Zhong Shu interview recording
occurrences.quote_span: Nolan has yet to respond directly, although, while being interviewed by podcaster Zhong Shu, he did speak out against “amateur criticism” for lacking the cinematic background essential for understanding the language of movies.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Emily Wilson

occurrences.checkable_against: Public commentary by Joyce Carol Oates and reactions to Wilson's film assessment
occurrences.quote_span: Her reaction to the film has been extensively — even obsessively — defended and denounced, including by Joyce Carol Oates, who faulted her “haughty superiority.”
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Emily Wilson

occurrences.checkable_against: Emily Wilson's interviews and London Review of Books assessment
occurrences.quote_span: In interviews with the AP and other media outlets, and in an assessment for the London Review of Books, she called the movie grandiose and superficial, and at times incoherent.
occurrences.speaker: Emily Wilson
occurrences.subject: Emily Wilson

occurrences.checkable_against: Contemporary reviews and online criticism of Wilson's 2017 translation
occurrences.quote_span: Wilson’s 2017 translation was praised by many critics for making “The Odyssey” feel more modern and accessible, but also faced criticism online for making the story “woke.”
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Emily Wilson

occurrences.checkable_against: 2017 edition publication records, sales records and contemporary coverage
occurrences.quote_span: Regarded as the first major English-language translation of Homer’s epic by a woman, her book was already a bestseller and a culture-wars flashpoint before the release of Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster adaptation.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Emily Wilson

occurrences.checkable_against: Publisher sales records for Emily Wilson's Odyssey
occurrences.quote_span: Her “Odyssey” has now sold more than a million copies, and Wilson has again become a reason to argue.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Emily Wilson

occurrences.checkable_against: Emily Wilson's interview statements and teacher adoption records
occurrences.quote_span: She says she’s “very much aware” that having two recent editions by the same translator would be a challenge for teachers, and hopes they won’t “curse” her name.
occurrences.speaker: Emily Wilson
occurrences.subject: Emily Wilson

occurrences.checkable_against: American Translators Association records of full-length retranslations
occurrences.quote_span: “I can’t really come up with a previous example of this situation,” says Kate Deimling, who oversees the literary division of the American Translators Association.
occurrences.speaker: Kate Deimling
occurrences.subject: Emily Wilson

occurrences.checkable_against: Publishing records for subsequent translator editions
occurrences.quote_span: “It’s not unheard of for translators to go back and make some corrections or edits in subsequent editions, but that’s not the same as a retranslation.”
occurrences.speaker: Kate Deimling
occurrences.subject: Emily Wilson

occurrences.checkable_against: Next edition manuscript of The Odyssey
occurrences.quote_span: Wilson, who says she will “probably” leave the line unchanged in the next edition, did not return his admiration.
occurrences.speaker: Emily Wilson
occurrences.subject: Emily Wilson

occurrences.checkable_against: Emily Wilson and her publisher's records for The Odyssey retranslation
occurrences.quote_span: If you’re among the many readers who learned to love “The Odyssey” through Emily Wilson’s 2017 translation, you might be surprised that she’s going to translate it again.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Emily Wilson

occurrences.checkable_against: Liveright Publishing communications about the retranslation
occurrences.quote_span: Asked how her publisher responded, Wilson says her decision was “very controversial.”
occurrences.speaker: Emily Wilson
occurrences.subject: Emily Wilson

occurrences.checkable_against: Emily Wilson's retranslation manuscript and University of Pennsylvania faculty records
occurrences.quote_span: “It’s a complete retranslation. It’s not a revision of the old version,” Wilson told The Associated Press during a recent Zoom interview from her home in Philadelphia, where she is a professor of classical studies at the University of Pennsylvania. “I’m about halfway through.”
occurrences.speaker: Emily Wilson
occurrences.subject: Emily Wilson

occurrences.checkable_against: Peter Simon's statement and the published new edition
occurrences.quote_span: Her editor at Liveright Publishing, Peter Simon, said in a statement that since she “has poured so much of her life and scholarship into ‘The Odyssey’ ... her new approach is bound to be thrilling.”
occurrences.speaker: Peter Simon
occurrences.subject: Emily Wilson
